circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, was designed by Hermann Tilke and has hosted the Formula One season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern venue for Formula One, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street layout encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various support categories. As an FIA Grade 1 licensed facility, it accommodates the premier motorsport event and related racing programmes on its permanent course.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the 4. 326 km circuit initially operated as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following modifications and a name change to the A1-Ring, the track returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is an urban racing venue situated along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, spanning 6. 003 km per lap to rank as the fourth-longest Formula One circuit. The track first hosted Formula One competition in 2016 with the European Grand Prix, before being designated as the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the inaugural Formula One race in the Middle East that same year. Beyond the annual F1 Grand Prix, the venue accommodates various motorsport disciplines including GP2 racing, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance competitions, holding an FIA Grade 1 license with multiple track configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657-kilometer circuit is renowned for its balanced blend of high-speed straights and technically demanding corners that test various aspects of driver skill. The FIA Grade 1-certified venue features spectator facilities accommodating over 140,000 fans.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The 7. 004 km Belgian circuit in the Wallonia region has been hosting Formula One racing since 1950, making it one of the sport's oldest venues. It currently stages the Belgian Grand Prix annually, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006 interrupting its regular calendar appearances since 1985.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometres and serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond hosting the premier racing series, the facility has welcomed various international motorsport competitions, including sportscar championships and North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport venue hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, with the race returning from 2024. The circuit has expanded its racing calendar to include electric vehicle racing events from 2024 onwards.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is a renowned English racing venue situated near Northamptonshire that has served as the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948. The circuit gained additional significance when it hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, though the British Grand Prix subsequently alternated among three different tracks before returning to Silverstone permanently from 1987 onwards. Beyond Formula One, the facility also stages the British MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km permanent facility near Budapest, hosted Formula One's historic 1986 debut in Eastern Europe. Built in just eight months starting in late 1985, it replaced plans for a Monaco-style street circuit and became the fastest-constructed Formula One venue to date.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's earliest purpose-built racing venue. The track is renowned as "the Temple of Speed" for its extended straightaways and fast-cornering sections, hosting the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949 except for a 1980 closure during renovation work.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, accommodating 155,000 spectators. The track hosts prestigious Formula One and Super Formula racing championships on its distinctive figure-eight layout.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track located in Paradise, Nevada, that navigates through the iconic Las Vegas Strip section of Boulevard. The course features numerous prominent landmarks including major hotels and casinos that line the racing route.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 304 km Mexico City circuit honours the Rodríguez brothers, both accomplished drivers who died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, following previous stints on an earlier configuration that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that hosts the Miami Grand Prix. Spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners, the track was specifically engineered by specialist circuit designers and achieves average qualifying speeds of approximately 139 mph in Formula One competition.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix takes place on a 3. 337 km street course that winds through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the harbor perimeter of the principality. Though officially named the Circuit de Monaco, the track is widely known as Monte Carlo since the majority of its layout occupies that neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit hosted the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix when it rejoined Formula One in 2021. The venue will continue on the calendar through 2025, with its sponsorship agreement set to conclude in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is positioned north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight, holding an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing venue in São Paulo, inaugurated in 1940 and renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his death in a 1977 aviation accident. The counterclockwise circuit hosts prestigious motorsport events and features an attached kart track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along the Red Sea waterfront in Saudi Arabia, serving as the home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in Formula One since its inaugural running in 2021. The layout has also begun hosting international electric racing competitions on the same prestigious waterfront location.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue situated around Singapore's Marina Bay, incorporating portions of the city's Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km circuit features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing skills. The venue accommodates nearly 141,000 spectators and holds the highest FIA safety certification grade.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 track that serves as the primary venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the facility hosts multiple motorsport series including NASCAR, MotoGP, and the FIA World Endurance Championship, establishing itself as a major racing destination in North America.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai and British driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, bringing two world championship titles earned with Renault in 2005 and 2006 along with 32 career Grand Prix victories. Beyond Formula One, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories with Toyota and the 2018–19 FIA World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both a Formula One drivers' title and a World Endurance drivers' championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured six Grand Prix victories since entering the championship in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently competing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that has included ten Grand Prix victories. He achieved back-to-back runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during 2019 and 2020 while competing for Mercedes.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines his European Le Mans Series commitments with a reserve role at Haas, having made seven Formula One race appearances during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a significant highlight of his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver with French and Algerian heritage, currently races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One while representing France.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding the joint-record of seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads in multiple statistical categories including race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi after building a career across multiple racing series. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved endurance racing success by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver competes for Ferrari and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine-season tenure in the sport. Leclerc finished second in the 2022 World Drivers' Championship while representing the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver known as K-Mag, competed in Formula One across two separate periods spanning from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024. Currently, he races in the FIA World Endurance Championship for BMW through WRT and also participates part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Across his eight-season career, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix victory with Alpine remains a highlight of his career.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio "Checo" Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 15-season career that has yielded six Grand Prix victories. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while competing for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver currently competing for McLaren, where he has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One over a 14-year period from 2011 through 2024, achieving eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British driver, competes for Mercedes in Formula One where he has secured seven race victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has claimed four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. He previously raced in Formula One between 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Canadian driver Lance Stroll currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, competing at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda held a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls during his Formula One tenure from 2021 through 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has claimed four consecutive Formula One World Championships between 2021 and 2024 while representing Red Bull Racing. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories under the Dutch flag.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently employed as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One, making him the sole competitor from China to have raced in the sport. He participated in Formula One competition across a three-year span from 2022 through 2024.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from its Enstone base as a French-licensed outfit, Alpine has competed in Formula One since 2021 following Renault's rebrand of its works team to promote the luxury sports car marque. The squad secured its only victory under the Alpine name when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, before Renault concluded its factory involvement at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has entered Formula One racing through multiple organizational structures, with the present iteration operating under AMR GP Limited as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury car manufacturer, represents the sport's most storied and victorious outfit, participating continuously in Formula One since the championship's inception in 1950. Nicknamed after their iconic emblem, the team has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the discipline's entire history, establishing itself as the sport's longest-running competitor.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the squad entering the sport in 2016. The team is currently led by principal Ayao Komatsu, following the departure of Guenther Steiner, who held the position since the team's establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, built both sports and Formula One cars as an independent manufacturer. The operation achieved significant endurance racing success including the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours victory before competing in Formula One from 1993 until 2025, making it the fourth-longest-serving constructor by race entries before being acquired by Audi to establish their new racing program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under the Mastercard sponsorship banner. Owned by the Bahraini investment firm Mumtalakat, the team operates as part of the broader McLaren Group structure.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through both factory teams and engine supply. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas operation, based in Brackley and holding a German racing licence, became a tripartite venture in January 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff. The marque's racing efforts have historically been associated with the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two teams under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as Red Bull's second constructors' entry in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, based in Faenza with operations near Milton Keynes. As one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing, it operates as a sister team within the broader Red Bull racing structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by Red Bull GmbH since its establishment in 2005. The team was led by Christian Horner throughout its two-decade history until his departure in 2025, when Laurent Mekies assumed the role of team principal.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One team and constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier unsuccessful racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name.
